# Vagdevi Food Products Private Limited — complete reference

> Vagdevi Food Products Private Limited is a rice miller and exporter at Yadgarpally, Miryalaguda, in the Nalgonda district of Telangana, India. Paddy is bought directly from farmers in the surrounding mandals and dried, milled, graded, colour-sorted and packed on a single ISO 22000:2018 certified site. The company supplies bulk buyers, private-label brands and export customers, and sells under its own Surya and Dwaraka brands.

Source: https://vagdevifoods.com. Generated from the website's own content on every deploy.

## Key facts

- Legal name: Vagdevi Food Products Private Limited (trading as Vagdevi Food Products / Vagdevi Foods)
- Incorporated: 15 September 2017

## Certifications and registrations

- **ISO 22000:2018** — certificate HYM/UAS/FMS/9186414/001, valid to 19 Jan 2027, issued by HYM International Certifications Pvt. Ltd. Food safety management covering processing, milling and export of rice and by-products. Certified since January 2018.
- **FSSAI State Licence** — licence no. 13618008000475, valid to 30 Dec 2028, issued by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. Issued by the Government of Telangana for the authorised premises at Yadgarpally, Miryalaguda.
- **APEDA RCMC** — registration 221976, valid to 31 Mar 2029, issued by Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). Registered as a Manufacturer Exporter of rice under the Foreign Trade Policy. IEC AAGCV1018C.

## How the business works

- **Same-day paddy.** Farmers from the surrounding mandals deliver straight to our gate. Nothing sits in a trader’s godown losing moisture and character before it reaches us.
- **One roof, one lot.** Drying, milling, grading, colour sorting and packing all happen on the same premises, so a lot number stays intact from weighbridge to warehouse.
- **Dispatch to seven states.** Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telangana and Odisha — with the Vijayawada highway and the Miryalaguda railhead at the door.

## Rice varieties

### JSR (Lachkari Kolam)

Our largest-selling grain and the rice inside the pink Surya pack. Cooks fluffy and separate, and holds its shape in pulao and everyday meals.

Available as: Steam Rice, Double Boiled Rice.

### HMT (Sona Masoori · Ponni type)

Fine, light and easily digestible. Sold as the black Surya pack and preferred wherever boiled rice is the daily staple.

Available as: Steam Rice, Double Boiled Rice.

### RNR (Telangana Sona)

A short-duration variety with a low glycaemic index, increasingly asked for by health-conscious households and institutional buyers.

Available as: Steam Rice, Double Boiled Rice.

### Pack sizes

- 10 kg — Retail shelf
- 26 kg — Household staple
- 30 kg — Kitchens & HoReCa

Woven PP and jute, printed to the buyer's artwork for private label, or in Vagdevi's own Surya and Dwaraka packs. Bulk consignments ship in 50 kg bags on request. Every pack carries a lot number tied to a milling date and a lab report.

### By-products

- **Rice Bran.** Drawn off at the polishing stage and sold on for oil extraction and cattle feed.
- **Broken Rice.** Graded fine and coarse, for food processing, brewing and feed applications.
- **Husk.** Used as boiler fuel, in board manufacture and as a soil conditioner.

## Brands

### Surya — "Love in every bite."

Pink for the north, black for the south. JSR Lachkari Kolam and HMT boiled, in 10, 26 and 30 kg packs — the rice that shows up on lakhs of plates across seven states.

### Surya Pink — JSR · Lachkari Kolam

The everyday cooker rice. Cooks fluffy and separate, never gluey — the grain that holds up in pulao, jeera rice and a plain dal-chawal night.

- Grain: Medium, slender
- Texture: Fluffy, separate
- Best for: Pulao · daily meals
- Packs: 10 · 26 · 30 kg
- Price: ₹3,000 per 26 kg bag, ₹3,460 per 30 kg bag

### Surya Black — HMT · Ponni type, boiled

Boiled rice for kitchens where rice is the meal, not the side. Soft, light and easy to digest — the one that goes with sambar, rasam and curd rice.

- Grain: Short, fine
- Texture: Soft, light
- Best for: Sambar · curd rice
- Packs: 10 · 26 · 30 kg
- Price: ₹3,000 per 26 kg bag, ₹3,460 per 30 kg bag

#### Surya pack colours

- **Pink** (JSR Lachkari Kolam, 10 · 26 · 30 kg): The flagship. Our highest-volume pack, strongest across the northern markets.
- **Black** (HMT boiled, 10 · 26 · 30 kg): Equal in volume to pink. The boiled-rice pack that moves through the south.
- **Dark green** (JSR steam, 26 · 30 kg): A steam-milled JSR for buyers who want the same grain without the boil.
- **Parrot green** (JSR steam, 26 · 30 kg): A second steam line kept for dealers who run two grades side by side.
- **Orange** (JSR, 26 · 30 kg): A regional favourite with a loyal pocket of kirana shops behind it.
- **Red** (JSR, 26 · 30 kg): Distinct on a crowded shelf, and easy for a repeat customer to point at.
- **Blue** (JSR, 26 · 30 kg): Runs in specific dealer territories where blue is the known Surya bag.
- **Silver** (JSR premium, 26 · 30 kg): The top of the range — the cleanest mill run of the season.

### Dwaraka — "The Taste of Tradition, The Promise of Quality."

Short, thick grain built for fermentation — idli and dosa batter that behaves the same way every single time.

## Exports

Registered with APEDA as a Manufacturer Exporter of rice (RCMC 221976, IEC AAGCV1018C).

- **Export-ready quality.** Moisture, whiteness, broken ratio and average length checked in-house, with a signed report per lot.
- **Private labelling.** Your artwork on 10, 26, 30 and 50 kg bags — the same lines that print Surya and Dwaraka.
- **Logistics from Miryalaguda.** On the Vijayawada highway with rail access, and reachable dry ports for container movement.

Indicative parameters. A signed lab report accompanies every shipment; custom specifications are quoted on request.

## Inside the mill: from a farmer's truck to a stitched bag

### 01. The gate — A truck arrives and is weighed before anything else

*Weighbridge, main gate.* Paddy comes in from farmers in the surrounding mandals and from mandi purchases. Nothing enters the yard unweighed — gross weight is recorded at the cabin, and the same bridge weighs the truck out empty so the net is beyond dispute.

- Recorded at: Gate cabin
- Weighed: In and out

### 02. The sample — A probe is pushed through the load, top to bottom

*Intake bay.* A sampling spear draws grain from several depths of the stack, not just the surface. That composite sample is what the lab reads — so a load cannot pass by having good paddy on top.

- Drawn from: Multiple depths
- Before: Unloading

### 03. The lab — Moisture, immature grain and foreign matter, on the spot

*Quality control room.* The sample is weighed and read while the truck waits. Loads outside our moisture band are turned back at the gate rather than argued about later. It is the least popular room in the mill and the most important one.

- Moisture band: 13–13.5%
- Decision: Accept / return

### 04. Unloading — Gunny by gunny into the intake pit

*Intake pit.* Accepted loads are emptied by hand into the pit, where an elevator lifts the paddy into the plant. The lot number is assigned here and it stays with that grain until it leaves as a stitched bag.

- Lot number: Assigned here
- Handling: Manual tip

### 05. Drying & silos — Held at a stable moisture through the whole season

*Dryers and steel silos.* Mechanical dryers bring paddy down to storage moisture, and MYSILO steel silos hold it there. This is why rice bought from us in April behaves like rice bought in November — the grain has not been sitting in a damp godown.

- Storage: Steel silos
- Drying: Mechanical

### 06. Milling — Hulled, then whitened on SATAKE lines

*Milling house.* The husk comes off first, then the bran, in stages rather than all at once — gentler on the grain and the reason our broken percentage stays low. Husk goes to the boiler; bran goes out for oil extraction.

- Whiteners: SATAKE
- Stages: Multi-pass

### 07. Polish & sort — Silky polished, graded, then colour sorted

*Grading floor.* Water-polished for finish, sieved to size, and passed through colour sorters that eject discoloured and immature grains. What comes off the end of the belt is what goes in the bag.

- Sorting: Optical
- Grading: By length

### 08. Bag & dispatch — Stitched, stacked, loaded, gone the same day

*Warehouse and loading yard.* Filled into 10, 26, 30 or 50 kg bags — ours or your printed artwork — stitched, stacked by lot, and loaded in the yard. Paperwork is issued the same day the truck leaves.

- Pack sizes: 10–50 kg
- Dispatch: Same day

### Plant and machinery

- **A 14-tonne boiler, fired on our own husk** (Steam generation). The husk taken off the paddy fuels the boiler that par-boils the next batch. Nothing is bought in to run it and nothing is dumped.
- **Paddy held in bulk, not in stacks** (Storage). A warehouse floor built to hold season-scale volume, so we buy when the farmer is selling rather than when the market forces us to.
- **Every stream on one plate** (Quality control). Paddy, brown rice, polished rice, broken and bran — drawn from the same lot and checked side by side before a consignment is cleared.

## Cooking Surya rice

### Pressure cooker

The everyday north-Indian default. Works for both packs; black needs one extra whistle. Best for: Pink JSR · Black HMT.

- Rice : water: 1 : 1¾
- Whistles: 3
- Rest: 5 min

1. **Rinse twice, not five times.** Two changes of water is enough to clear loose starch. Over-rinsing washes off the surface layer that gives Surya its aroma.
2. **Soak 20 minutes.** Cuts cooking time and helps every grain swell evenly rather than splitting at the ends.
3. **Three whistles, medium flame.** Add 1¾ cups water per cup of rice. Switch off at the third whistle — the residual pressure finishes the job.
4. **Rest before you open.** Five minutes with the lid on. Fluff with a fork, never a spoon, so the grains stay whole.

### Open pot

How boiled rice is cooked across the south — drain the starch and the grains stay separate. Best for: Black HMT · boiled.

- Rice : water: 1 : 4
- Boil: 12–14 min
- Drain: Yes

1. **Bring water to a rolling boil first.** Rice goes into boiling water, not cold. Four parts water per part rice gives it room to move.
2. **Boil uncovered, 12 to 14 minutes.** Test at twelve: the grain should crush between two fingers with a faint firmness in the middle.
3. **Drain the starch water.** Tip into a colander. Keep the kanji — it is the best thing to drink with a hot meal.
4. **Steam-dry for two minutes.** Return to the empty pot off the heat, lid ajar. The surface moisture leaves and the grains separate.

### Rice cooker

For hostel rooms and small kitchens. Set it and forget it — the ratio does the work. Best for: Pink JSR.

- Rice : water: 1 : 1½
- Cycle: Auto
- Rest: 10 min

1. **Rinse in the inner pot itself.** Two rinses, then level the rice with your palm so it cooks evenly across the base.
2. **One and a half parts water.** Less than a cooker needs — a rice cooker loses almost no steam, so extra water turns it sticky.
3. **Let it switch to keep-warm.** Do not lift the lid mid-cycle. The cooker knows when the water is gone.
4. **Ten minutes on keep-warm.** This is the step everyone skips. It finishes the centre of the grain.

### Biryani & pulao

JSR holds its shape under layering and dum better than a long-grain basmati at twice the price. Best for: Pink JSR.

- Cook to: 70%
- Soak: 30 min
- Dum: 15 min

1. **Soak a full 30 minutes.** Longer soak, shorter boil. The grain elongates instead of breaking when you layer it.
2. **Par-boil to seventy percent.** In salted water with a bay leaf and cloves. The grain should still resist at the core.
3. **Layer while hot, seal the pot.** Rice over masala, saffron milk and fried onion on top. Seal with dough or a tight lid and a weight.
4. **Dum on the lowest flame, 15 minutes.** Use a tawa under the pot. Rest another ten minutes before you open it at the table.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where is the Vagdevi Food Products rice mill?

The mill is at Sy. Nos. 328–333, Vijayawada Road, Yadgarpally, Miryalaguda, Nalgonda district, Telangana 508207 — inside the Nagarjuna Sagar command area, the rice bowl of Telangana. The registered office is at Jain Sadguru Capital Park, Madhapur, Hyderabad.

### Which rice varieties does Vagdevi Food Products mill?

Three varieties, each available as steam rice or double boiled rice: JSR (Lachkari Kolam), HMT (Sona Masoori, Ponni type) and RNR (Telangana Sona). The mill also sells rice bran, broken rice (fine and coarse) and husk.

### What pack sizes are available?

10 kg, 26 kg and 30 kg packs in woven PP or jute, plus 50 kg bags for bulk consignments on request. Every pack carries a lot number that ties it back to a milling date and a lab report.

### Do you pack rice under a private label?

Yes. Vagdevi Food Products prints your artwork on 10, 26, 30 and 50 kg bags, on the same lines that pack its own Surya and Dwaraka brands.

### Is the mill certified?

Yes. ISO 22000:2018 (certificate HYM/UAS/FMS/9186414/001, valid to 19 Jan 2027), FSSAI State Licence 13618008000475 (valid to 30 Dec 2028) and APEDA RCMC 221976 as a Manufacturer Exporter of rice (valid to 31 Mar 2029). The Import Export Code is AAGCV1018C.

### Does Vagdevi Food Products export rice?

Yes. The company is registered with APEDA as a Manufacturer Exporter of rice (RCMC 221976) and supplies importers, wholesalers and private-label brands. Moisture, whiteness, broken ratio and grain length are checked in-house, and a signed lab report goes with every lot.

### Which states do you supply?

Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telangana and Odisha, dispatched from Miryalaguda with the Vijayawada highway and the Miryalaguda railhead at the door.

### How much does Surya rice cost?

Surya rice costs ₹3,000 for a 26 kg bag and ₹3,460 for a 30 kg bag — about ₹115 per kg. The pink pack is JSR Lachkari Kolam; the black pack is HMT boiled rice.

### How do I get a bulk rice quote?

WhatsApp or call the sales desk on +91 90004 16808, Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm IST, with the variety, quantity and delivery city. The reply comes with a price, a lab report and a dispatch date. You can also email info@vagdevifoods.com.

### Can buyers visit the mill?

Yes. Buyers are welcome to walk the plant at Yadgarpally before they order — message the sales desk on WhatsApp with a preferred date and it will be arranged.

### How do farmers sell paddy to Vagdevi Food Products?

Farmers bring paddy straight to the procurement hall at the mill. Weight, moisture and payment are settled on the same visit, and the money goes directly into the farmer's bank account. Bring your pattadar passbook, bank passbook and Aadhaar. For payment queries call 95504 16809.
